pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


When you first start following Jesus, you learn about freedom. You learn that Jesus sets you free. You learn that Jesus breaks the chains. You learn that Jesus delivers you from sin. It is wonderful. It is life-changing. It is the good news.


But then you open the Old Testament. You read about slavery in Egypt. You read about the Exodus. You read about the Promised Land. You read about heroes who delivered people. You might wonder, "What does this have to do with my freedom? How does this connect to my new life?"


Here is the secret. The Old Testament is a rescue plan. It is a blueprint. It is a preview. Every hero. Every deliverer. Every rescue. They all point to the ultimate rescue. They all point to Jesus. They all point to your freedom.


This book is for you. You are new to the faith. You are building your foundation. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 Old Testament heroes. We are going to see how they rescued people. We are going to see how they set people free. And we are going to see how they point to your freedom in Christ.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament as just a collection of old stories. You will see it as a rescue plan. You will see it as a blueprint. You will see it as a preview. You will understand the Old Testament heroes. You will understand their rescues. You will understand why they matter for your freedom. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the one who is the ultimate rescue.


How to Use This Guide


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 5 to 10 minutes. Read the promise. Read the proof. Read why it matters for your new life. Read ...

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD." - Genesis 6:8 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Noah found favor. He found grace. He found mercy. God told him to build an ark. God told him to build a rescue. Noah obeyed. He built the ark. He saved his family. He saved the animals. He was a rescuer. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit." - 1 Peter 3:18


Jesus is the greater Noah. Noah built an ark. Jesus is the ark. Noah saved his family. Jesus saves the world. Noah found favor. Jesus is the favor. Noah was a rescuer. Jesus is the ultimate rescuer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a rescue. You might need a safe place. You might need an ark. Remember Noah. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the ark. He is the safe place. He is the rescue. You are safe in Him.


Faith Builder
Draw a picture of a boat. Write the name "Jesus" on it. Thank Him for being your ark. Thank Him for rescuing you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my ark. Thank you for being my rescue. Thank you for saving me. Help me to trust in your rescue. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 1: Noah the Rescuer

The Proof (NT)
"This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham..." - Matthew 1:1


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham was blessed. Jesus is the blessing. Abraham was promised a family. Jesus is the fulfillment of the promise. Abraham was a blessing. Jesus is the ultimate blessing.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a blessing. You might need a rescue. You might need a future. Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the blessing. He is the rescue. He is the future. You are blessed through Him.


Faith Builder
Think of one way you can be a blessing to someone this week. Write it down. Ask God to help you do it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for the blessing. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that I am blessed through Him. Help me to be a blessing to others. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.

The Proof (NT)
"Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.'" - Luke 23:34


Jesus is the greater Joseph. Joseph forgave his brothers. Jesus forgave his enemies. Joseph saved many lives. Jesus saved the world. Joseph was a forgiver. Jesus is the ultimate forgiver.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to forgive someone. You might have been hurt. You might have been betrayed. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. They forgave. They forgave their enemies. You can forgive too.

The Prayer

The Proof (NT)
"It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery." - Galatians 5:1


Jesus is the greater Moses. Moses delivered the Israelites. Jesus delivers us. Moses set them free. Jesus sets us free. Moses was a deliverer. Jesus is the ultimate deliverer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to be delivered. You might need to be set free. You might need to be led out. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They delivered. They set free. They led out. Jesus can deliver you. Jesus can set you free.


Faith Builder

The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the deliverer. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He delivered me. Help me to live in your freedom. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.

Jesus is the greater Rahab. Rahab was a sinner. Jesus was a savior. Rahab was an outsider. Jesus brings outsiders in. Rahab was saved. Jesus saves. Rahab was a rescuer. Jesus is the ultimate rescuer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life

The Prayer

Jesus is the greater Samuel. Samuel listened to God. Jesus listened to the Father. Samuel heard God's voice. Jesus heard the Father's voice. Samuel was a listener. Jesus is the ultimate listener.

Why It Matters For Your New Life

The Prayer

Jesus is the greater Jonah. Jonah ran away. Jesus obeyed. Jonah was in the fish for three days. Jesus was in the tomb for three days. Jonah was a reluctant rescuer. Jesus is the ultimate rescuer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life

Faith Builder

The Prayer

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But if I say, 'I will not mention his word or speak anymore in his name,' his word is in my heart like a fire, a fire shut up in my bones. I am weary of holding it in; indeed, I cannot." - Jeremiah 20:9 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Jeremiah was a weeping prophet. He wept for his people. He wept for their sin. He wept for their future. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"As he approached Jerusalem and saw the city, he wept over it..." - Luke 19:41


Jesus is the greater Jeremiah. Jeremiah wept for his people. Jesus wept for his people. Jeremiah spoke for God. Jesus is God. Jeremiah was a weeping rescuer. Jesus is the ultimate weeping rescuer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might weep for your family. You might weep for your friends. You might weep for the world. Remember Jeremiah. Remember Jesus. They wept. They cared. They loved. You can weep too.


Faith Builder
Think of someone who needs your prayers. Write their name down. Ask God to help you weep for them.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Jeremiah. Thank you for the weeping. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He wept for me. Help me to weep for others. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: Jeremiah the Weeping

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel; so hear the word I speak and give them warning from me." - Ezekiel 3:17 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Ezekiel was a watchman. He watched for danger. He warned the people. He spoke for God. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour." - Matthew 25:13


Jesus is the greater Ezekiel. Ezekiel was a watchman. Jesus is the watchman. Ezekiel warned the people. Jesus warns the people. Ezekiel was a watchman rescuer. Jesus is the ultimate watchman rescuer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to be a watchman. You might need to warn someone. You might need to speak the truth. Remember Ezekiel. Remember Jesus. They watched. They warned. You can watch too.


Faith Builder
Think of someone you can warn this week. Write their name down. Ask God to give you the words to say.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Ezekiel. Thank you for the watchman. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He warns me. Help me to be a watchman. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: Ezekiel the Watchman

pages.title: Day 23: Hosea the Faithful Husband

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"The LORD said to me, 'Go, show your love to your wife again, though she is loved by another man and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods...'" - Hosea 3:1 (Written around 750 B.C.)


Hosea was a faithful husband. He loved his wife. He loved her even when she was unfaithful. He loved her even when she ran away. He loved her even when she broke his heart. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us." - Romans 5:8


Jesus is the greater Hosea. Hosea loved an unfaithful wife. Jesus loves an unfaithful world. Hosea forgave his wife. Jesus forgives us. Hosea was a faithful husband. Jesus is the ultimate faithful husband.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have been unfaithful. You might have run away. You might have broken God's heart. Remember Hosea. Remember Jesus. They loved. They forgave. They restored. Jesus loves you. Jesus forgives you. Jesus restores you.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "Jesus loves me even when I fail." Say it out loud. Thank Him for His faithful love.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the faithful husband. Thank you for loving me even when I fail. Thank you for forgiving me. Thank you for restoring me. Help me to love you. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: Hosea the Faithful Husband (Continued)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"I will repay you for the years the locusts have eaten—the great locust and the young locust, the other locusts and the locust swarm—my great army that I sent among you." - Joel 2:25 (Written around 800 B.C.)


Joel was a restorer. He spoke of restoration. He spoke of repayment. He spoke of renewal. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose." - Romans 8:28


Jesus is the greater Joel. Joel spoke of restoration. Jesus brings restoration. Joel spoke of repayment. Jesus repays. Joel was a restorer. Jesus is the ultimate restorer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have lost years. You might have lost opportunities. You might have lost time. Remember Joel. Remember Jesus. They restore. They repay. They renew. Jesus can restore your lost years.


Faith Builder
Think of a year you feel you have lost. Write it down. Ask Jesus to restore it. Thank Him for being the restorer.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the restorer. Thank you for restoring my lost years. Thank you for repaying what the locusts have eaten. Help me to trust your restoration. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: Joel the Restorer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!" - Amos 5:24 (Written around 750 B.C.)


Amos was a justice bringer. He spoke of justice. He spoke of righteousness. He spoke of fairness. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For he has set a day when he will judge the world with justice by the man he has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising him from the dead." - Acts 17:31


Jesus is the greater Amos. Amos spoke of justice. Jesus brings justice. Amos spoke of righteousness. Jesus is righteousness. Amos was a justice bringer. Jesus is the ultimate justice bringer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might long for justice. You might long for fairness. You might long for righteousness. Remember Amos. Remember Jesus. They bring justice. They bring righteousness. Jesus will bring justice.


Faith Builder
Think of an injustice you have seen. Write it down. Ask Jesus to bring justice. Thank Him for being the justice bringer.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the justice bringer. Thank you for bringing justice. Thank you for bringing righteousness. Help me to trust your justice. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: Amos the Justice Bringer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But on Mount Zion will be deliverance; it will be holy, and Jacob will possess his inheritance." - Obadiah 1:17 (Written around 850 B.C.)


Obadiah was a deliverer. He spoke of deliverance. He spoke of rescue. He spoke of salvation. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the greater Obadiah. Obadiah spoke of deliverance. Jesus brings deliverance. Obadiah spoke of rescue. Jesus brings rescue. Obadiah was a deliverer. Jesus is the ultimate deliverer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need deliverance. You might need rescue. You might need salvation. Remember Obadiah. Remember Jesus. They deliver. They rescue. They save. Jesus can deliver you.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "Jesus is my deliverer." Say it out loud. Thank Him for delivering you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the deliverer. Thank you for delivering me. Thank you for rescuing me. Thank you for saving me. Help me to live in your deliverance. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: Obadiah the Deliverer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times." - Micah 5:2 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Micah was a promiser. He spoke of a promise. He spoke of a ruler. He spoke of a king. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"So Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem the town of David, because he belonged to the house and line of David." - Luke 2:4


Jesus is the greater Micah. Micah promised a ruler. Jesus is the ruler. Micah promised a king. Jesus is the king. Micah was a promiser. Jesus is the ultimate promiser.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a promise. You might need a hope. You might need a king. Remember Micah. Remember Jesus. They promised. They fulfilled. They ruled. Jesus is your king.


Faith Builder
Write down one promise from God you are holding onto. Say it out loud. Thank Jesus for being the fulfillment of the promise.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the fulfillment of the promise. Thank you for being the ruler. Thank you for being the king. Help me to trust your promises. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: Micah the Promiser

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his foes and vents his wrath against his enemies." - Nahum 1:2 (Written around 650 B.C.)


Nahum was an avenger. He spoke of vengeance. He spoke of justice. He spoke of wrath. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God's wrath, for it is written: 'It is mine to avenge; I will repay,' says the Lord." - Romans 12:19


Jesus is the greater Nahum. Nahum spoke of vengeance. Jesus brings vengeance. Nahum spoke of justice. Jesus brings justice. Nahum was an avenger. Jesus is the ultimate avenger.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need vengeance. You might need justice. You might need someone to fight for you. Remember Nahum. Remember Jesus. They bring vengeance. They bring justice. Jesus will fight for you.


Faith Builder
Think of someone who has hurt you. Write their name down. Give them to Jesus. Let Him be the avenger.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the avenger. Thank you for bringing justice. Thank you for fighting for me. Help me to trust your justice. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: Nahum the Avenger

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"How long, LORD, must I call for help, but you do not listen? Or cry out to you, 'Violence!' but you do not save?" - Habakkuk 1:2 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Habakkuk was a questioner. He asked God questions. He asked God why. He asked God how long. He was a rescuer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the greater Habakkuk. Habakkuk asked questions. Jesus answered questions. Habakkuk cried out. Jesus answered. Habakkuk was a questioner. Jesus is the ultimate answer.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have questions. You might have doubts. You might have fears. Remember Habakkuk. Remember Jesus. He asked. He answered. You can ask Jesus your questions.


Faith Builder
Write down a question you have for God. Ask Him. Then listen. Write down what you sense He is saying.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the answer. Thank you for answering my questions. Thank you for listening to me. Help me to trust you. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: Habakkuk the Questioner

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But the LORD said to Moses, 'I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians. I will free you from being slaves to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.'" - Exodus 6:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Old Testament is full of rescues. Noah was rescued. Abraham was blessed. Joseph was forgiven. Moses was delivered. Rahab was saved. Joshua conquered. Gideon was mighty. Samson was strong. Ruth was redeemed. Samuel listened. David slew giants. Solomon was wise. Elijah was a prophet. Elisha healed. Jonah was reluctant. Daniel was faithful. Esther was brave. Nehemiah built. Job was patient. Isaiah spoke. Jeremiah wept. Ezekiel watched. Hosea loved. Joel restored. Amos brought justice. Obadiah delivered. Micah promised. Nahum avenged. Habakkuk questioned. All of them were rescuers. All of them were heroes. All of them point to Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the ultimate rescue. He is the one who came to seek. He is the one who came to save. He is the one who came to rescue. He is the fulfillment of every rescue. He is the fulfillment of every hero. He is the ultimate rescue.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You have been rescued. You have been saved. You have been delivered. You have been set free. Remember the rescue. Remember the hero. Remember Jesus. He is the ultimate rescue.


Faith Builder
Write down one thing you have learned about the rescue over the last 30 days. Thank God for the rescue. Thank Him for Jesus.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the rescue. Thank you for the heroes. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for the ultimate rescue. Help me to live in the rescue. Help me to follow the ultimate rescuer. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Rescue Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 days of the rescue plan. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every rescue. As you read, look for the rescue. Look for the hero. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The rescues are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The rescues point to a person. The rescues point to Jesus. You can understand the rescues and still miss the ultimate rescue. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The rescues are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. loves helping new believers build a strong foundation. He believes that faith is not a blind leap. It is a confident step based on evidence. He lives with his family and enjoys hiking and reading.


Coming Next: The Great Parallel
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Great Parallel takes a 30 day look at meeting Jesus in the Old Testament. It is for the new believer who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of believers. The journey is not over. The adventure is just beginning.



Cover Design Concept (The New Believer Edition)


A soft, warm cream or light parchment background. A large, glowing scroll sits in the center. On the scroll, a series of figures is drawn in simple, friendly lines. Noah with his ark. Moses with his staff. David with his sling. Esther with her crown. They are all smiling. They are all pointing to a cross in the center. The title THE RESCUE PLAN is in a strong, trustworthy, bold serif font. The subtitle is in a gentle, welcoming sans-serif. The overall feel is warm, inviting, and full of hope.
